requirement.text: The system is designed and architecture is planned privacy and data protections auditability in mind. Clear documentation on how API and services joining the SMART terminal system will affect the privacy and data Protection.

analysis.ethical_objective: Ensure privacy and data protection are considered in system design and architecture, and make the privacy and data-protection effects of APIs and services joining the SMART terminal system clearly documented.
stakeholders: Organizations using or integrating with the SMART terminal system
explicit_requirements: The system design must take privacy and data protection into account.
The system architecture planning must take privacy and data protection into account.
The system design and architecture must take auditability into account.
Clear documentation must describe how APIs joining the SMART terminal system affect privacy and data protection.
Clear documentation must describe how services joining the SMART terminal system affect privacy and data protection.
supported_implications: Privacy and data protection must be addressed during both design and architecture planning, rather than only after implementation.
Auditability is a design and architecture consideration.
Integration-related privacy and data-protection impacts must be made available through documentation.
The documentation applies to both APIs and services that join the SMART terminal system.
constraints: Applies to the SMART terminal system.
Applies when APIs or services join the SMART terminal system.
The required documentation concerns effects on privacy and data protection.
The source requires consideration of privacy, data protection, and auditability but does not prescribe specific controls or mechanisms.
ambiguities: The meaning and scope of 'auditability' are not defined.
The specific privacy and data-protection impacts that must be documented are not identified.
It is unclear whether documentation is intended for integrators, users, operators, or another audience.
It is unclear what qualifies an API or service as 'joining' the system.
The source does not specify the format, location, timing, or maintenance expectations for the documentation.
The relationship between privacy and data protection is not further defined.
unsupported_assumptions_to_avoid: Do not assume particular privacy controls, such as encryption, consent management, access controls, anonymization, or data minimization.
Do not assume audit logs, logging formats, retention periods, or audit procedures are required.
Do not assume a privacy impact assessment or formal approval process is required.
Do not assume APIs and services must be approved, blocked, monitored, or technically assessed before joining the system.
Do not assume specific documentation formats, templates, publication channels, update schedules, or target audiences.
Do not assume legal, regulatory, or standards-based compliance obligations.
possible_operational_aspects: Privacy and data-protection considerations in system design.
Privacy and data-protection considerations in architecture planning.
Auditability considerations in system design and architecture planning.
Documentation describing privacy and data-protection effects of joining APIs.
Documentation describing privacy and data-protection effects of joining services.

initial_draft.title: Privacy-Aware and Auditable Integration Design
initial_draft.description: As an organization integrating with the SMART terminal system, I want clear documentation of how joining APIs and services affect privacy and data protection, so that I can assess their privacy and data-protection implications.
work_items: The SMART terminal system’s design and architecture planning shall take privacy and data protection into account.
The SMART terminal system’s design and architecture planning shall take auditability into account.
Clear documentation shall describe the effects of APIs joining the SMART terminal system on privacy and data protection.
Clear documentation shall describe the effects of services joining the SMART terminal system on privacy and data protection.

criterion_support.criterion: Role: an organization integrating with the SMART terminal system
supported_by: The requirement concerns APIs and services joining the SMART terminal system; an integrating organization is a suitable stakeholder perspective, although the intended documentation audience is not specified.
criterion_support.explanation: The role is a plausible, focused stakeholder for integration documentation and does not add a substantive obligation.

criterion_support.criterion: Goal: clear documentation of the privacy and data-protection effects of joining APIs and services
supported_by: “Clear documentation on how API and services joining the SMART terminal system will affect the privacy and data Protection.”
criterion_support.explanation: The goal preserves the documentation obligation and its scope.

criterion_support.criterion: Reason: assess privacy and data-protection implications
supported_by: The source requires documentation of effects on privacy and data protection.
criterion_support.explanation: Assessing the disclosed effects is a direct informational use of the documentation and does not introduce a broader unsupported benefit.

criterion_support.criterion: Work item 1: system design and architecture planning take privacy and data protection into account
supported_by: “The system is designed and architecture is planned privacy and data protections ... in mind.”
criterion_support.explanation: This preserves the source obligation to consider privacy and data protection during design and architecture planning.

criterion_support.criterion: Work item 2: system design and architecture planning take auditability into account
supported_by: “The system is designed and architecture is planned ... auditability in mind.”
criterion_support.explanation: This preserves auditability as a design and architecture planning consideration without inventing an audit mechanism.

criterion_support.criterion: Work item 3: documentation describes effects of joining APIs on privacy and data protection
supported_by: “Clear documentation on how API ... joining the SMART terminal system will affect the privacy and data Protection.”
criterion_support.explanation: This directly represents the API portion of the documentation requirement.

criterion_support.criterion: Work item 4: documentation describes effects of joining services on privacy and data protection
supported_by: “Clear documentation on how ... services joining the SMART terminal system will affect the privacy and data Protection.”
criterion_support.explanation: This directly represents the services portion of the documentation requirement.

unresolved_issues: Work items 3 and 4 are substantially redundant and should be consolidated while retaining coverage of both APIs and services.

The source does not define what it means for design and architecture planning to take privacy, data protection, and auditability into account; this limits the precision and verifiability of those conditions.

issues.problem: The API and service documentation work items express the same obligation separately, creating unnecessary duplication.
issues.recommended_change: Combine the closely related documentation conditions into one work item that explicitly covers both APIs and services joining the SMART terminal system.

issues.problem: The requirement to take privacy, data protection, and auditability into account does not specify what considerations, outcomes, or criteria demonstrate satisfaction.
issues.recommended_change: No additional specificity should be added unless it is available from the authoritative source; retain the source-level consideration requirement and recognize its inherent interpretive limitation.

issues.problem: The source provides no defined indicators, controls, or criteria for verifying that privacy, data protection, and auditability were taken into account in design and architecture planning.
issues.recommended_change: Do not invent verification criteria, mechanisms, or thresholds. Any improvement in testability requires source-provided definitions or acceptance conditions.
